claims.text: Differences in mechanical properties among equiatomic Cr-Mn-Fe-Co-Ni and its quaternary and ternary subsets arise from variations in local lattice distortion.
Differences in mechanical properties among the alloys arise from variations in dislocation density.
The combination and proportion of alloying elements influence local lattice distortion.
The combination and proportion of alloying elements influence dislocation density.
Local lattice distortion affects dislocation mobility and interactions.
Dislocation density affects dislocation mobility and interactions.
Changes in dislocation mobility and interactions lead to differences in mechanical properties.
The quinary Cr-Mn-Fe-Co-Ni alloy will have higher strength than its quaternary and ternary subsets.
The quinary Cr-Mn-Fe-Co-Ni alloy will have greater resistance to deformation than its quaternary and ternary subsets.
The ternary subsets will have lower ductility than the quinary baseline.
The ternary subsets will be more susceptible to failure than the quinary baseline.
The comparison is restricted to equiatomic alloys that are single-phase FCC after thermomechanical processing.
A lack of correlation between mechanical-property differences and measured lattice distortion or dislocation density would falsify the hypothesis.
